title: Rigveda 10.109: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.109: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.109 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 95r-95v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.109.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 6, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 95r
translation.original_text:
1te̍ 'vadan pratha̱mā bra̍hmakilbi̱ṣe 'kū̍pāraḥ sali̱lo mā̍ta̱riśvā̍ | vī̱ḻuha̍rā̱s tapa̍ u̱gro ma̍yo̱bhūr āpo̍ de̱vīḥ pra̍thama̱jā ṛ̱tena̍ ||
2somo̱ rājā̍ pratha̱mo bra̍hmajā̱yām puna̱ḥ prāya̍ccha̱d ahṛ̍ṇīyamānaḥ | a̱nva̱rti̱tā varu̍ṇo mi̱tra ā̍sīd a̱gnir hotā̍ hasta̱gṛhyā ni̍nāya ||
3haste̍nai̱va grā̱hya̍ ā̱dhir a̍syā brahmajā̱yeyam iti̱ ced avo̍can | na dū̱tāya̍ pra̱hye̍ tastha e̱ṣā tathā̍ rā̱ṣṭraṁ gu̍pi̱taṁ kṣa̱triya̍sya ||
translation.text:
1THESE first, the boundless Sea, and Mâtariṣvan, fierce-glowing Fire, the Strong, the Blissbestower. And heavenly Floods, first-born by holy Order, exclaimed against the outrage on a Brahman.
2King Soma first of all, without reluctance, made restitution of the Brahman's consort. Mitra and Varuṇa were the inviters: Agni as Hotar took her hand and led her.
3The man, her pledge, must by her hand be taken when they have cried, She is a Brahman's consort. She stayed not for a herald to conduct her: thus is the kingdom of a ruler guarded.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 95r (OPenn image 94, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.108.11 ‹paṇayo varīya ud gāvo›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 95v, begins in RV 10.109.4 ‹-avadanta pūrve saptaṛṣayas tapase›. Verses 10.109.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.109.4-7 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 6, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 95v
translation.original_text:
4de̱vā e̱tasyā̍m avadanta̱ pūrve̍ saptaṛ̱ṣaya̱s tapa̍se̱ ye ni̍ṣe̱duḥ | bhī̱mā jā̱yā brā̍hma̱ṇasyopa̍nītā du̱rdhāṁ da̍dhāti para̱me vyo̍man ||
5bra̱hma̱cā̱rī ca̍rati̱ vevi̍ṣa̱d viṣa̱ḥ sa de̱vānā̍m bhava̱ty eka̱m aṅga̍m | tena̍ jā̱yām anv a̍vinda̱d bṛha̱spati̱ḥ some̍na nī̱tāṁ ju̱hva1̱̍ṁ na de̍vāḥ ||
6puna̱r vai de̱vā a̍dadu̱ḥ puna̍r manu̱ṣyā̍ u̱ta | rājā̍naḥ sa̱tyaṁ kṛ̍ṇvā̱nā bra̍hmajā̱yām puna̍r daduḥ ||
7pu̱na̱rdāya̍ brahmajā̱yāṁ kṛ̱tvī de̱vair ni̍kilbi̱ṣam | ūrja̍m pṛthi̱vyā bha̱ktvāyo̍rugā̱yam upā̍sate ||
translation.text:
4Thus spake of her those Gods of old, Seven R̥ishis who sate them down to their austere devotion: Dire is a Brahman's wife led home by others: in the supremest heaven she plants confusion.
5The Brahmachâri goes engaged in duty: he is a member of the Gods' own body. Through him Br̥ihaspati obtained his consort, as the Gods gained the ladle brought by Soma.
6So then the Gods restored her, so men gave the woman back again. The Kings who kept their promises restored the Brahman's wedded wife,
7Having restored the Brahman's wife, and freed them, with Gods' aid, from sin, They shared the fulness of the earth, and won themselves extended sway.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 95v (OPenn image 95, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.109.4 ‹-avadanta pūrve saptaṛṣayas tapase›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 96r, begins in RV 10.110.1 ‹tvaṁ dūtaḥ kavir asi›. Verses 10.109.4-7 end on this page; 10.109.4 begins on fol. 95r.
